title: What Makes a Bird
objective: After this level you can explain feathers, beaks and hollow bones.
summary: Feathers set birds apart from every other animal. Birds also have toothless beaks, lay hard-shelled eggs and make their own heat, and big fliers carry bones partly filled with air.

cards.headline: A frigatebird's skeleton weighs less than its feathers.
cards.body: That's a bird with a seven-foot wingspan, and its bones are outweighed by its coat. It sounds like a trick. It's actually a clue to what a bird is, and to how so many of them manage to be so light.

cards.headline: Feathers are the password
cards.body: Not every bird can fly, so flight can't be the test. The real password is feathers. Britannica calls them the major characteristic that sets birds apart from all other animals. A turtle has a beak, but no turtle has a single feather. If it grows feathers, it's a bird. Full stop.

mascot.line: Keep this: feathers are the test, not flight. Level 30's ostrich can't fly and is still a bird.

cards.headline: The rest of the kit
cards.body: Every bird is a vertebrate, one of the five backbone groups from Level 3. Its beak is its upper and lower jaws wrapped in a horny sheath, and no bird has teeth. Every bird lays hard-shelled eggs. And like you, birds make their own heat (Level 5), holding steady at about 40 °C. Feathers, beak, eggs, inner furnace: that's the kit.

cards.fact: In big fliers, the bones are partly air.
cards.context: In the largest flying birds, part of the bone is replaced by air spaces. A hollow tube can buckle, though, so the big wing bones carry struts inside, like the cross-braces in a bridge. That's how a frigatebird with a seven-foot wingspan ends up with a skeleton lighter than its feathers.

cards.headline: Birds: defined
learned: Feathers: the one trait only birds have
Toothless beaks: jaws in a horny sheath
Hard-shelled eggs and an inner furnace near 40 °C
Big fliers have air-filled, strut-braced bones

questions.prompt: Which feature does Britannica single out as what separates birds from all other animals?

options.label: Wings
options.rationale: Not every bird flies, so wings can't be the test.

options.label: Hollow bones
options.rationale: Only some bird bones are partly air; feathers are the password.

questions.explanation: Feathers are the major characteristic that distinguishes birds from all other animals.

questions.prompt: Why do the big wing bones of large flying birds have struts inside them?

options.label: To keep the hollow bones from buckling
To store fat for long flights
options.rationale: The spaces hold air; the struts add strength.

options.label: To make the bones heavy for diving
To anchor the bird's feathers
options.rationale: The struts are about strength, not feathers.

questions.explanation: Partly hollow bones save weight, and internal struts keep their walls from buckling.

questions.prompt: Level 5 sorted animals by where their heat comes from. Where do birds fit?

options.label: Ectotherms that bask to reach 40 °C
options.rationale: Basking is how ectotherms warm up; birds heat themselves.

options.label: Endotherms, but only while flying
options.rationale: They hold a steady temperature whatever the weather.

questions.explanation: Birds are endotherms: like mammals they make their own heat, holding about 40 °C.
